deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page continues the previous one: 'Reduction der Zone 1794. 25 März auf 1815 Jun 30'. Gauss takes a declination zone from 1794 March 25, apparently from Lalande's Histoire Céleste. He corrects its clock zero with known stars (Cor Caroli, 17 Canum Venaticorum). He then reduces two anonymous 8th-magnitude zone stars to apparent places for 1815 June 30, presumably as comparison stars for a moving object observed then. The object is not named on the page; Olbers' comet of 1815 is only a guess. Time units: 1794 March 25 is 1794.230 and 1815 June 30 is 1815.496, so t = 21.266 years.

BLOCK 1 (17 Canum, check of the zone's clock correction).
- Catalogue mean place, apparently epoch 1800: alpha = 195°12'40.00", delta = +39°33'56.80".
- Precession back to 1794.23 (about 5.77 years): -4'0.55" in RA and +1'51.71" in declination. Result: 195°8'39.45", +39°35'48.51".
- Mean to apparent place for 1794 March 25.
  - RA: aberration +23.83", nutation (alpha-independent part) -9.53", nutation (alpha-dependent part) -5.40". Result: 195°8'48.35".
  - Dec: aberration alpha-part -1.88", aberration constant part -6.18", nutation +6.05". Result: +39°35'46.50".
- Converted to time: 195°8'48.35"/15 = 13h0m35.22s. The zone gave 13h0m34.98s, hence the clock correction +0.24s listed on p.281.

GAUSS'S AUXILIARY-ANGLE FORM OF ABERRATION AND NUTATION (my reconstruction, verified numerically).
- Sun longitude 0s5°32' (= 5.53°), lunar node 4s24°50' (= 144.83°), obliquity e about 23°28'.
- Aberration: define A, Theta' by A cos Theta' = k cos(Sun) cos e and A sin Theta' = k sin(Sun), with k = 20.25".
  - This gives Theta' = 6°2' and log A = 1.2694.
  - d(alpha) = -A cos(alpha - Theta') sec(delta).
  - d(delta) = -A sin(Theta' - alpha) sin(delta) - k cos(Sun) sin(e) cos(delta).
- Nutation: define B, node' by B cos(node') = c1 cos(node) and B sin(node') = c2 sin(e) sin(node).
  - The coefficients come out c2 about 18.0" and c1 about 9.6"; this gives node' = 152°19' and log B = 0.9497.
  - d(alpha) = -c2 sin(node) cos(e) - B cos(alpha - node') tan(delta).
  - d(delta) = -B sin(node' - alpha).
- Log columns for alpha = 195°9' (all checked):
  - Column 1: 1.2694n + 9.9945n + 0.1132 = 1.3771, i.e. +23.83.
  - Column 2: 1.2694n + 9.1999 + 9.8044 = 0.2737n, i.e. -1.88.
  - Column 3: 0.9497n + 9.8653 + 9.9176 = 0.7326n, i.e. -5.40.
  - Column 4: 0.9497n + 9.8324n = 0.7821, i.e. +6.05.

BLOCK 2 (two zone stars).
- Apparent places from the corrected zone (p.281):
  - Star a: 12h14m43.89s = 183°40'58.35", +39°27'27.41".
  - Star b: 12h15m14.90s = 183°48'43.50", +39°29'24.45".
- Apparent to mean place, with one set of terms computed for alpha = 183°45' and used for both stars.
  - RA: -24.07 + 9.53 + 6.26 = -8.28". Logs: 1.2694n + 9.9997n + 0.1124 = 1.3815; 0.9497n + 9.9311 + 9.9156 = 0.7964n.
  - Dec: -0.47 + 6.19 - 4.65 = +1.07". Logs: 1.2694n + 8.6003n + 9.8032 = 9.6729; 0.9497n + 9.7173n = 0.6670.
- Mean places 1794.23:
  - a: 183°40'50.07", +39°27'28.48".
  - b: 183°48'35.22", +39°29'25.52".
- Precession to 1815.496. log t = 1.32768 (t = 21.266 years); log m = 1.66313 (m = 46.03"/yr); log n = 1.30242 (n = 20.06"/yr).
  - m t: log 2.99081, i.e. 16'19.06".
  - n t: log 2.63010, i.e. 426.7".
- Gauss applies the precession as two successive rotations.
  - First add m t: a 183°57'9.13", b 184°4'54.28".
  - Dec change n t cos(alpha), with alpha taken after the m t step. Logs 2.63010 + 9.99897n (a) and 2.63010 + 9.99890n (b). Results -7'5.67" and -7'5.60".
  - RA change n t sin(alpha) tan(delta), with alpha taken about midway and the mean delta.
  - Star a: 2.63010 + 8.83804n = 1.46814n; plus tan 9.91454 (corrected from 9.91469) gives -24.14".
  - Star b: 2.63010 + 8.85199n = 1.48209n; plus 9.91504 gives -24.95".
- Mean places 1815.5:
  - a: 183°56'44.99", +39°20'22.81".
  - b: 184°4'29.33", +39°22'19.92".

BLOCK 3 (mean to apparent place for 1815 June 30).
- Sun 3s8°20', node 3s3°35'. Theta' = 97°39', node' = 94°47', alpha = 184°4.5'. log A = 1.3058, log B = 0.8570.
- RA: -1.63 (1.3058n + 8.7949 + 0.1118 = 0.2125n), -16.51 (nutation constant part), -0.07 (0.8570n + 8.0921 + 9.9141 = 8.8632n). Total -18.21".
- Dec: +12.80 (1.3058n + 9.9992n + 9.8023 = 1.1073), +2.99, -2.08, +7.19 (0.8570n + 0.0000n = 0.8570). Total +20.90".
- Final apparent places 1815 June 30:
  - a = 183°56'26.78", +39°20'43.71".
  - b = 184°4'11.12", +39°22'40.82".
- The marginal 'Süd/Nord...' fragment belongs to the facing braid page.
errors: No substantive arithmetic errors were found; all additions, log sums and time conversions check to 0.01" or one unit in the last log place.

Dec column of 1815: the terms +2.99 and -2.08 are not individually identified. Their sum, +0.91, equals the expected constant aberration term -k cos(Sun) sin(e) cos(delta) = +0.90". The split may be a slip-and-correction or a term I cannot identify.

The log tan(delta) for star a was first written 9.91469 and corrected to 9.91454; the correction is right, since tan(39°23.9') gives log 9.91453. The log sin entry 8.83804n is overwritten but consistent with alpha near 183°56'54".
Applying the precession as an m t rotation followed by an n t tilt, with alpha+mt used in cos(alpha), is a first-order approximation. Here its error is under 0.1" because sin(alpha) is small.
The nutation coefficients implied, about 18.0" and about 9.6", are the older values of the period, not modern ones (17.2", 9.2"). This is not an error for 1815.
log B = 0.9497 for 1794 and 0.8570 for 1815 imply slightly differing coefficient pairs. This is a minor inconsistency, at most 0.05" in effect.

results.what: Reduction of star places mean to apparent (annual aberration plus nutation), written with auxiliary angles Theta' and node' so each correction is a single log product
results.usually_credited_to: Bradley (aberration, nutation); tabular auxiliary-angle forms by Gauss, Zach, Bessel (Tabulae Regiomontanae 1830)

results.what: Precession over 21.27 years with annual constants m = 46.03" and n = 20.06"
results.modern_name: General precession in RA and Dec (first-order formulas)

results.what: Determination of a zone's clock zero from known stars (17 CVn, Cor Caroli) and reduction of Lalande zone stars to 1815

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine positional-astronomy bookkeeping (precession, aberration, nutation) of the kind Gauss did constantly at Göttingen. There is nothing mathematically novel.

checkable.asserts: Theta' is about 6.03° (6°2') for Sun longitude 5°32'
log of the RA aberration is about 1.3771, i.e. 23.83"
n t sin(alpha) tan(delta) is about 24.14"
the corrected log tan 9.91454 is right
log cos(alpha - Theta') is about 8.7949 for 1815
the constant aberration term in Dec for 1815 is about +0.90", matching +2.99-2.08

transcription_corrections: The crossed-out entry in the star-a precession column is written '8.83804n' (first digits overwritten); the transcription's '8.8[-3804-]n' should read 8.83804n. It is the log sin(alpha) for star a, distinct from 8.85199n for star b.
The small '1922' above Theta = 3.8.20 is of unclear meaning and is possibly not a number belonging to the computation.
The top-right triplets '6°2' / 152.19 / 195.9' and '6°2' / 152.19 / 183.45' are Theta', node' and alpha (195°9', 183°45') used in the log columns.
The marginal fragments 'Süd... Nord... 1 2 ... Mit.' belong to the facing page (braid study), not to this computation.
